advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Wire tests/external/test_bedrock_cache_live.py into the Bedrock arm (add the `_live_llm_ready` sentinel / migrate it onto the shared `_live_llm` gate) or explicitly document why it stays out, so the credentialed Bedrock arm actually exercises the Bedrock cache canary.
evidence: tests/external/test_bedrock_cache_live.py:28: `pytestmark = pytest.mark.external` — module makes a REAL Bedrock call but defines no `_live_llm_ready` sentinel

tests/external/test_bedrock_cache_live.py:30: `_skip = pytest.mark.skipif(os.environ.get("REBAR_LIVE_BEDROCK", "")... )` — self-skips unless REBAR_LIVE_BEDROCK is set, which the workflow never sets in any job
tests/external/conftest.py:70: `_SENTINEL_MARKERS = {"_live_jira_ready": "jira_live", "_live_llm_ready": "llm_live"}` — only modules exposing `_live_llm_ready` are auto-marked `llm_live`
external-integration.yml:219: bedrock arm runs `pytest -m "external and llm_live"`; this module is `not llm_live` so the arm never collects it

external-integration.yml:243-371: the `external` services job (which runs the `not llm_live` complement) configures no `configure-aws-credentials`/OIDC step and no AWS region, so this test would fail there even if REBAR_LIVE_BEDROCK were set
tests/unit/test_ci_provider_matrix.py:381: the sentinel guard test only inspects modules where `"_live_llm" in text`, so it does not flag this Bedrock-live module
advisory.finding: The live Bedrock cache canary tests/external/test_bedrock_cache_live.py is excluded from the new Bedrock arm and never runs in CI: it lacks the `_live_llm_ready` sentinel so it is not auto-marked `llm_live`, so `-m "external and llm_live"` (external-llm bedrock arm) skips it, while the `external` services job runs `-m "external and not llm_live"` but sets no AWS/OIDC credentials and the test self-skips on `REBAR_LIVE_BEDROCK` (never set in the workflow). The Bedrock cache/`cachePoint` regression it exists to detect remains undetectable by CI even after this change adds a credentialed Bedrock arm — the exact goal of the story.
scenarios: A Bedrock prompt-cache wiring regression in pydantic-ai or rebar's capabilities.py/providers.py ships and CI stays green because the canary that would catch it runs in no job.
An operator relying on the new matrix to shorten the Bedrock-regression detection window is unaware this specific canary is not wired in.
advisory.suggested_fix: Migrate test_bedrock_cache_live.py onto the shared `_live_llm` gate (define `_live_llm_ready = _live_llm.live_llm_ready()` and use `@_live_llm.skip_without_live_llm`, driving the model off the resolved standard/frontier class), so it is auto-marked `llm_live` and runs inside the credentialed Bedrock arm; drop the standalone REBAR_LIVE_BEDROCK gate or keep it as an additional narrowing only if intended.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add unit tests for tests/external/_live_llm.py (configured_provider prefix/default, credential_present per-provider/generic/Bedrock branches, _skip_reason wording) with boto3 and env monkeypatched.
evidence: `search_files _live_llm in tests/unit` returns only the sentinel-presence grep at test_ci_provider_matrix.py:381 — no unit test imports or exercises the module's functions
tests/external/_live_llm.py:116 `return agents_extra_installed() and credential_present(configured_provider())` — the gate every live module applies
tests/external/_live_llm.py:63-69 configured_provider partitions the resolved 'standard' string on ':' and falls back to DEFAULT_PROVIDER — untested parsing/fallback logic
tests/external/_live_llm.py:80-86 credential_present has a Bedrock->boto3 branch, a generic-key branch, and a per-provider env branch, none unit-covered

ABSENCE: a mis-detection here (e.g. Bedrock credential_present True when boto3 resolves nothing, or a wrong provider prefix) reintroduces the exact 'arm skips every test and reports green' failure the story removes, and would only surface on the next scheduled/dispatched billable CI run
advisory.finding: The new tests/external/_live_llm.py readiness probe — the story's central provider-resolution and credential-detection mechanism — has no unit test; its branches (configured_provider prefix parsing + default fallback, credential_present per-provider/generic-key/Bedrock-boto3 paths, _skip_reason) are exercised only indirectly inside a live CI arm, which is the slow/billable feedback loop tests/unit/test_ci_provider_matrix.py explicitly exists to short-circuit.
scenarios: boto3 chain resolves no Bedrock credentials but _aws_credentials_resolvable mis-reports True, so live_llm_ready is True and tests run/fail unexpectedly — or vice versa, every test skips and the arm greens
resolve_model_string returns a string whose prefix parsing regresses, mapping the wrong provider's credential check
advisory.suggested_fix: Add tests/unit/test_live_llm_probe.py importing tests/external/_live_llm as a standalone module (as test_external_canary.py loads the conftest), monkeypatching os.environ and boto3.session.Session().get_credentials() to assert each provider's credential_present result and configured_provider's parsing/fallback.

dropped.checklist_item: - [ ] Consider narrowing the Bedrock CI role trust `sub` to `refs/heads/main` (or an `environment:bedrock-ci` scope with required-reviewer gating) rather than `refs/heads/*`, since the scheduled trigger only needs the default branch.
evidence: infra/runbooks/bedrock-ci-oidc.md:70 `"token.actions.githubusercontent.com:sub": "repo:navapbc/rebar:ref:refs/heads/*"`
infra/runbooks/bedrock-ci-oidc.md:91-95 `\`refs/heads/*\` means *anyone who can push a branch to the GitHub mirror* can run a workflow that assumes this role. That is deliberate...`

external-integration.yml:31-38 triggers are only `workflow_dispatch: {}` and `schedule: - cron: "0 6 * * 1"` — a scheduled run's OIDC subject is the default-branch ref, so branch-wildcard is required only for dispatch from a non-main branch
infra/runbooks/bedrock-ci-oidc.md:99-102 offers tighter `main-only` and `environment-scoped` variants but the JSON/HCL default remains `refs/heads/*`
dropped.finding: The Bedrock CI role's recommended trust policy scopes the OIDC `sub` condition to `repo:navapbc/rebar:ref:refs/heads/*` (ANY branch), which is broader than the workflow's actual trigger surface requires and lets anyone who can push a branch to the mirror assume the role and incur Bedrock token spend. The workflow triggers only on `workflow_dispatch` and a weekly `schedule`; scheduled runs always execute on the default branch, so the branch wildcard is needed solely for dispatch-from-a-non-main-branch. The runbook itself documents this as residual risk and offers tighter `main-only` / `environment-scoped` variants, but presents the widest scope as the operator's default.
scenarios: A contributor with branch-push access dispatches the external suite from an arbitrary branch and assumes the Bedrock role
A compromised branch triggers billable Converse calls
